goal: The pinned `ga mail` grant in the guard has behavioural tests for chained commands, so a regression that opens Bash fails a test, not only a golden byte compare.
why: BD-268: in guard_py.py mail(), dropping `len(parts) > 2` is caught only by golden-byte tests; the mutant returns 'pinned' for `ga mail send … --guard-event F && rm -f F && curl evil.example`, which would open Bash.

scope.text: Behavioural tests (not golden bytes) for mail(): three or more parts chained with &&; each of ';', '||' and '|' after an otherwise pinned `ga mail send … && rm -f F`; each must return 'unpinned'. Keep the existing pinned case passing.
Change code only if a new test shows a real hole; otherwise tests only.

done_when.text: With golden-byte tests excluded, the mutation 'drop len(parts) > 2' is killed, and a mutation that accepts ';' / '||' / '|' after the pinned command is killed; name the tests.
Full suite green in a fresh clone; report as report/2 in English on #15 with the commit sha.
